findings_addressed.oracle: Independent sort oracle via httpx.MockTransport injected at the network boundary. Stub serves two model records in strict reverse-alphabetical order (zeta-sort-b before alpha-sort-a). The expected sorted sequence is derived independently as sorted([m.name for m in models]). The assertion is unconditionally evaluated because the stub always delivers exactly two records — no if-guard, no vacuous loop, no environment-dependent skip. Element-type oracle: every item must be isinstance(item, ModelInfo).
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/providers/ollama.py, change the final line of OllamaProvider.list_models() from 'return sorted(models, key=lambda m: m.name)' to 'return models'. The stub delivers models with zeta-sort-b first and alpha-sort-a second, so the unsorted return produces names=['[Local] zeta-sort-b', '[Local] alpha-sort-a'], which differs from the independently computed sorted list ['[Local] alpha-sort-a', '[Local] zeta-sort-b'] and makes the assertion fail unconditionally.

notes: G0273 re-hardened by replacing the environment-dependent live-API test (which was vacuous on 0-1 models and non-falsifiable on alphabetically-ordered installs) with a stub-transport gate. An httpx.MockTransport is injected via monkeypatch at OllamaProvider._build_local_client — the sole external network boundary — so the production parsing pipeline, sort call, and ModelInfo construction all execute unmodified. The stub delivers two records in descending name order; the production sorted() call must reorder them to ascending to pass the assertion. This eliminates all N6 (conditional/vacuous), N8 (existence-only), and environment-dependent weaknesses identified by the adversarial reviewer.
